openings: Our class is making a small display.
We want to show our work to our families.
There is space for a display near our classroom.
situations: We need a clear plan before we begin.
We have many pictures to choose from.
Everyone wants to help with the display.
actions: We put the pictures into groups and write simple labels.
We choose our favorite drawings and arrange them on the board.
We ask our teacher to help us choose a good order.
results: The display is easy to read when we finish.
Each picture has a place where people can see it.
We stand back and check the whole board together.
reflections: We are proud to share something we made together.
Working as a team makes the task more enjoyable.
We learn that a small plan can save time.

openings: My cousin is visiting our town.
We are planning a short walk with our friends.
Our family wants to explore a different part of town.
situations: We need a route that everyone can follow.
There are several interesting places near the square.
We want to see something new without walking too far.
actions: We look at a map and mark the places we want to visit.
We choose a path that goes past the market and the park.
We ask a neighbor to suggest a quiet street to explore.
results: Our route has places where we can stop and rest.
The plan gives us time to look around slowly.
Everyone knows where the walk will begin and end.
reflections: I am looking forward to showing our visitors around.
A familiar town can still have new things to discover.
Planning the walk together is part of the fun.

openings: We need more space for our books.
There is an empty shelf in the classroom.
Our reading corner needs some attention.
situations: Some books are difficult to find.
We have books about many different subjects.
People often ask where the storybooks belong.
actions: We sort the books by subject and add small labels.
We put the storybooks together and make a sign for each section.
We ask the class to help us arrange the books neatly.
results: The books are much easier to find now.
There is a clear place for every kind of book.
We can see which books we might like to read next.
reflections: We agree to put each book back after reading it.
Keeping a shared space tidy helps everyone.
A little work can make a room feel more welcoming.

openings: Our friends are coming over for lunch.
We are preparing a meal for our family.
My brother and I want to help in the kitchen.
situations: We need to decide what food to prepare.
There are useful ingredients in the cupboard.
We want to make something simple that everyone can share.
actions: We check the ingredients and write a short shopping list.
We choose a simple recipe and divide the jobs between us.
We ask an adult to help us plan the meal.
results: Everyone has a clear job to do before lunch.
The kitchen is ready for us to start cooking.
We know which ingredients we need and which we already have.
reflections: It is easier to cook when we plan together.
Helping with a meal is a good way to learn.
We are excited to share the food when it is ready.

openings: We are writing a guide for new students.
Our school wants to welcome some new pupils.
The teacher asks us to describe our school.
situations: New students need to know where things are.
We remember how confusing the school seemed on our first day.
There are several useful places to include in the guide.
actions: We draw a simple map and add the names of the rooms.
We write short directions and ask a friend to check them.
We make a list of useful places and explain how to find them.
results: The guide answers some common questions about the school.
Our directions are short enough to read quickly.
We have a useful page to give to new students.
reflections: We hope the guide will help someone feel at home.
Clear words can make a new place less confusing.
We enjoy making something useful for other people.

openings: We want to start a reading club.
Some friends enjoy talking about books.
The library has a quiet corner for a small group.
situations: We need to choose a book for our first meeting.
Our group includes people who like different stories.
We want everyone to feel comfortable joining the discussion.
actions: We look at several short books and choose one together.
We ask the librarian to suggest a book we can all borrow.
We share our favorite kinds of stories before choosing a book.
results: We agree on something interesting to read before the meeting.
Everyone knows which book we will discuss first.
Our first reading choice gives us something to look forward to.
reflections: There is no need to read quickly to enjoy a good story.
We are interested in hearing what other readers notice.
A book can be even more enjoyable when we talk about it.

openings: Our class is helping at the school fair.
We are planning a small stall for a school event.
Our group wants to make something for the fair.
situations: We need to decide what visitors might enjoy.
We have a small table and some craft materials.
Everyone has an idea for the stall.
actions: We choose a simple craft and make a few examples.
We compare our ideas and write down what each one needs.
We ask our teacher which ideas will fit our table.
results: We have a clear idea of what to prepare.
Our plan uses the space and materials we have.
Each person knows how to help before the fair.
reflections: We want visitors to feel welcome at our stall.
Listening to each other helps us make a better plan.
We are looking forward to working together on the day.

openings: We find a box of old family photographs.
My grandmother brings out an old photo album.
Our family is looking through some pictures from the past.
situations: Some photographs do not have names or dates.
We want to remember who is in each picture.
The pictures show places that look different now.
actions: We ask our relatives about the photographs and write down their answers.
We sort the pictures into groups and add careful notes.
We look at the photographs together and record the stories we hear.
results: The pictures are easier to understand with their new notes.
We have learned more about the people in the photographs.
Our notes help connect the pictures with family memories.
reflections: We want to keep these memories safe for the future.
An old photograph can begin an interesting conversation.
I enjoy learning about the lives of my relatives.
